title: Scandium Recovery from Bauxite Residue: Leaching Selectivity, Precursor Qualification, and Residue Management
content: This review compares scandium recovery from Bayer residues, sinter-derived residues, and feeds modified by alkali fusion or reductive treatment. It distinguishes extraction into liquor, downstream recovery, and production of specification-compliant scandium oxide. A worked comparison for a sinter-derived feed shows that increasing leach pH from 2 to 4 reduced scandium extraction from more than 80% to 63.5%, while dissolved iron per gram of scandium fell by about 176-fold. An illustrative precursor iron limit shows when a lower-extraction liquor merits priority in purification trials. Mineralogical evidence helps select which leach conditions to test, while feed-specific mass balances are needed to distinguish selective release from impurity reprecipitation. Route comparisons must include fresh reagent and water demand, pretreatment energy, purification losses, and management of filter cake and liquid rejects. Evidence gaps in these quantities prevent a general ranking of routes by circularity.
